title: Cardiac Health in Breast Cancer (CHiB): a single center, randomized-controlled trial
summary: Breast cancer is becoming more common, with 2.3 million new cases per year and a 5-year survival rate that has improved to 90%. However, this longer survival means that more patients may experience long-term side effects from their treatments, including cancer therapy-related heart problems (CTRCD). The “Cardiac Health in Breast Cancer” (CHiB) study aims to determine whether a structured exercise program can reduce the risk of heart damage in breast cancer patients undergoing cardiotoxic treatment. In this study, 48 women will be randomly assigned to either a one-year exercise program featuring HIIT and HIRT or to a control group. The primary goal is to assess whether exercise can lower the risk of heart dysfunction due to cancer therapy, while also evaluating heart inflammation, quality of life, and other health factors.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Planned cardiotoxic chemotherapy with adjuvant or neoadjuvant intention
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy, contraindications to MRI examinations (e.g. claustrophobic complaints, ferromagnetic implants), a glomerular filtration rate < 30 ml/min or pre-existing cardiovascular disease (heart failure, a cardiac arrhythmia requiring treatment, coronary heart disease, a past pulmonary artery embolism, previous cardiac surgery or a congenital heart defect). Orthopaedic and functional conditions that do not permit sporting activity
